description: Open-source, self-hosted AI language learning platform with local or cloud LLMs, CEFR study plans, an AI tutor, voice conversations, flashcards, and spaced repetition.

latest_release.name: v1.14.10
latest_release.body:
## [1.14.10] - 2026-11-17

### Added

- Add Everyday situations to Practice with 50 voice role-plays across five personal and work themes, including straightforward everyday exchanges, translated titles and descriptions, search, category filtering, and locale-aware ordering. Each situation gives Lingu a concrete role and objective adapted to the learner's study plan, with concise interaction and a natural conclusion after meaningful practice.
- Add a configurable Situations allowance of one start per account/ISO week through `FREEMIUM_SITUATIONS_WEEKLY`, preserving existing voice access and limits. Situations use the current voice conversation, transcript history, and plan-owned vocabulary saves.

### Changed

- Align the Games catalog header with Everyday situations, using an open title and description layout with matching typography and responsive spacing.
- Give OpenAI TTS the same female/male selector as Gemini, with independent provider preferences and backend-configurable voices. Default to `gpt-4o-mini-tts` with `female` mapped to `marin` and `male` to `cedar`; ignore saved provider-name preferences until a new choice is selected. Validate voice/model compatibility and refresh on-demand audio caches when mapped voices change, including with legacy OpenAI models.
- Give Gemini TTS explicit pronunciation and regional-accent guidance for every supported language, sharing OpenAI's instructions while preserving the selected voice and multilingual text. Refresh on-demand audio caches when those instructions change.

### Fixed

- Prevent daily lessons from returning a server error after a generation or persistence rollback. Reuse concurrent lesson inserts safely and continue remaining slots without losing committed lessons or progress.

# FreeLingo [![Hosted](https://img.shields.io/badge/hosted%20service-available-green?style=flat-square)](https://freelingo.app) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL%20v3-blue?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/next.js-16-black?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.14-blue?style=flat-square) [![Self-hosted](https://img.shields.io/badge/self--hosted-yes-orange?style=flat-square)](#quick-start) ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.14.10-brightgreen?style=flat-square) **Structured learning. Everyday practice. Conversations with Lingu.** [Try FreeLingo Cloud](https://freelingo.app) · [Self-host](#quick-start) · [Development](DEVELOPMENT.md) · [Sponsor](https://github.com/sponsors/artcc)
## Overview FreeLingo is an open-source language learning platform with a structured A1–C2 curriculum and an AI tutor, **Lingu**. Use the managed service or run the application on your own infrastructure. 1. **Find your starting point.** Take the adaptive placement quiz or start at A1 as a beginner. Quiz scoring and study-plan scheduling are deterministic; the plan follows the selected language's curriculum, level, and duration of 4, 8, 12, or 16 weeks. 2. **Follow your plan.** Work through curriculum units with clear competencies and prerequisites. Lesson content is AI-generated within those boundaries, with native-language explanations and practice across grammar, vocabulary, comprehension, and writing. 3. **Practise with Lingu.** Use text and voice tutoring with user-controlled memories. Completed lessons also offer voice practice: confirm a topic preview, then discuss the lesson with help informed by your exercise answers. These conversations retain the existing voice limits and appear in chat history under the lesson topic. Alongside the plan: - **Review and explore:** SM-2 flashcards, grammar and vocabulary resources, a phrasebook, generated Listening and Reading exercises, and pronunciation practice. - **Practise grammar topics:** add references to a [personal grammar library](specs/grammar-practice.instructions.md), complete saved five-question practices, and track results across plans in the same language. Completed practices can continue in voice with Lingu, informed by the topic and your answers. - **Rehearse everyday situations:** choose from 50 [voice role-plays](specs/situations.instructions.md) across daily life, travel, shopping and services, social life, and work. Practise a concrete objective with Lingu at your study plan's language and level. - **Learn through games:** [Error Detective, Sentence Order, and Vocabulary Pairs](specs/games.instructions.md). Review completed lessons, prepare familiar foundations for the next lesson, or practise at your plan's level. Sessions are saved for later, with language-specific history and plan-owned XP; freemium access uses a shared daily game quota. - **See your progress:** XP, streaks, skill scores, unit competencies, and end-of-level tests. The dashboard highlights today's XP, seven days of activity, and plan progress. Rewards recognise lessons, reviews, meaningful tutor participation, and unit/level completion; activity uses UTC dates. - **Learn multiple languages:** keep separate plans, progress, flashcards, and learning attempts for each study language. Account settings, subscription, quotas, and tutor memories remain global. [Architecture](#architecture) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Configuration](#operational-notes) · [Speech setup](#configuring-tts--stt) ## Hosted service > **FreeLingo Cloud — start learning without managing a server.** > > Visit **[freelingo.app](https://freelingo.app)** for the managed service, with a free plan and paid > subscriptions. No Docker, GPU, or server maintenance required from the learner. The hosted instance is operated by the FreeLingo team. **Self-hosting remains free and open source** under AGPL-3.0; you manage your deployment and its infrastructure/provider costs. Accounts and progress belong to each installation. ## For businesses Need FreeLingo for your team or organisation? - **Private / on-premise deployment:** run FreeLingo on your infrastructure and control configuration, storage, and provider selection. - **Dedicated managed instance:** setup, hosting, maintenance, and updates for your organisation in a dedicated environment. - **Commercial licence:** deploy a customised or white-labelled version under separately agreed terms. See [COMMERCIAL_LICENSE.md](COMMERCIAL_LICENSE.md). [Get in touch](https://freelingo.app) via the contact form to discuss your requirements. Support continued development through [**GitHub Sponsors**](https://github.com/sponsors/artcc). ## Architecture The monorepo combines a **Next.js frontend** and a **FastAPI backend**, deployed with Docker Compose. - **Frontend:** presentation, navigation, and browser audio capture/playback. - **Backend:** business logic, authentication, persistence, and all LLM, TTS, and STT integrations. - **Storage:** PostgreSQL 16 for durable application data; Redis 7 for sessions and operational state. The frontend never calls AI or speech providers directly. See [the architecture specification](specs/architecture.instructions.md) for system structure and [the Docker specification](specs/docker.instructions.md) for runtime and image details. ## Repository
Browse the project structure ```text freelingo/ ├── assets/ # Logos and static assets ├── backend/ # FastAPI (Python) ├── blender/ # Lingu source model and animations ├── data/ # Shared data files ├── docs/ # GitHub Pages landing site ├── frontend/ # Next.js (React) ├── messages/ # Interface translation catalogs ├── scripts/ # Local toolchain, formatting, and validation ├── specs/ # Specification files ├── AGENTS.md # AI assistant instructions ├── CHANGELOG.md # Version history ├── CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md # Community guidelines ├── COMMERCIAL_LICENSE.md # Commercial licence terms ├── CONTRIBUTING.md # Contribution guidelines ├── CONTRIBUTOR_LICENSE_AGREEMENT.md # CLA for contributors ├── DEVELOPMENT.md # Local development setup ├── docker-compose.yml # Production deployment ├── docker-compose.dev.yml # Development deployment ├── LICENSE # AGPL-3.0 licence ├── README.md # This file └── run-dev.sh # Development helper script ```
## Stack - **Frontend:** Next.js 16, shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS, Zustand, next-intl - **Backend:** FastAPI, SQLAlchemy async, Alembic, Pydantic v2 - **Data:** PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 7 - **LLM:** Ollama, OpenAI, Anthropic, or DeepSeek - **Speech:** Kokoro-FastAPI, OpenAI, or Gemini TTS; faster-whisper or OpenAI Whisper - **Auth:** JWT access and refresh tokens with admin/user roles - **Deployment:** Docker Compose ## Quick start Choose **[Docker Compose](#option-a--git-clone--docker-compose)** for a command-line deployment or **[Portainer](#option-b--portainer-stack)** for stack management. **Server prerequisites** - Docker and Docker Compose; Git for the clone-based setup. - A supported cloud LLM API or [Ollama](https://ollama.com). - An NVIDIA GPU for the default local speech containers, or cloud speech credentials (OpenAI for STT; OpenAI or Gemini for TTS). - For production voice: HTTPS and reverse-proxy routing for `/ws/*`, as explained [below](#reverse-proxy-requirement-real-time-conversation). Choose your [speech providers](#configuring-tts--stt) before starting the stack. The default Compose file includes GPU containers for both local speech services; selecting a cloud provider in `.env` does not disable those containers automatically. ### Option A — Git clone + Docker Compose **1. Clone and configure** ```bash git clone https://github.com/artcc/freelingo.git cd freelingo cp .env.example .env ``` Edit `.env`: configure `DATA_PATH`, database and Redis credentials, `SECRET_KEY`, and your LLM and speech providers. Review the remaining settings in [.env.example](.env.example). **2. Prepare the model — only when using Ollama** On the Ollama host, run `ollama pull` with the model configured in `OLLAMA_MODEL`. **3. Start the stack** ```bash docker compose up -d ``` Pending database migrations run automatically each time the backend starts. Open the frontend on localhost or your server's address using the host port published in `docker-compose.yml`. Production microphone access requires the HTTPS setup described below. `FIRST_USER_IS_ADMIN` controls whether the first registered user becomes an administrator. Review it in `.env` before opening registration. ### Option B — Portainer (Stack) 1. Open Portainer → **Stacks** → **Add stack**. 2. Choose **Repository** and enter the repo URL, or paste the contents of `docker-compose.yml` directly into the Web editor. 3. Add the variables from `.env.example`. At minimum, configure `DATA_PATH`, the `POSTGRES_*` values, `REDIS_PASSWORD`, `SECRET_KEY`, and the selected LLM and speech providers and credentials. 4. Click **Deploy the stack**. 5. Access the app at your server's address and the frontend host port published in the stack. Database migrations run automatically when the backend starts. > **Ollama on the same host:** point `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` to the host's Ollama listener, using > `host.docker.internal` and its configured port. > On Linux, if that hostname does not already resolve, add `host.docker.internal:host-gateway` > under the backend's `extra_hosts`. Production Compose does not include this mapping. ## Operational notes ### AI providers - **Language model:** `LLM_PROVIDER` selects `ollama`, `openai`, `anthropic`, or `deepseek`. Configure the selected provider's model and credentials through `.env`; see [.env.example](.env.example). - **Speech:** `TTS_PROVIDER` selects `local` (Kokoro), `openai`, or `gemini`; `STT_PROVIDER` independently selects `local` (faster-whisper) or `openai`. See [speech setup](#configuring-tts--stt).
OpenAI and Anthropic model settings - OpenAI LLM requests use the **Responses API**, with the model selected by `OPENAI_MODEL`. The selected model and endpoint must support Responses; a Chat Completions-only gateway is insufficient. FreeLingo manages conversation context and sends `store=false`. - Optional `OPENAI_REASONING_EFFORT` applies to OpenAI chat, memory-tool turns, and content generation. Leave it empty for the model default. Values are `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`, subject to model support; there are no model-specific overrides. - Ollama and DeepSeek use Chat Completions; Anthropic uses its native API. - `ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS` must fit the selected model's output limit. See the [service contracts](specs/services.instructions.md) for provider behavior.
### Limits and access Conversation, token, freemium, and trial limits are configurable in [.env.example](.env.example). See [subscriptions and quotas](specs/subscriptions-freemium.instructions.md) for scope and access rules. Web subscriptions use Stripe Checkout. Optional `REVENUECAT_ENABLED=true` synchronizes a shared Premium entitlement through RevenueCat while retaining Stripe payments and the existing web interface. It requires `STRIPE_ENABLED=true`, provider credentials, webhook configuration, and importing existing subscriptions before activation. See the [RevenueCat setup and operating contract](specs/subscriptions-freemium.instructions.md#revenuecat-configuration-and-operation) and [.env.example](.env.example). ### Study languages Choose from 20 study languages, counting each regional variant separately, and learn one or several side by side. Each has its own A1–C2 curriculum, placement test, grammar reference, vocabulary and phrasebook. - **Chinese:** Mainland Mandarin, in simplified characters (`zh-CN`). - **Croatian:** Croatia (`hr-HR`). - **Czech:** Czechia (`cs-CZ`). - **Danish:** Denmark (`da-DK`). - **Dutch:** Netherlands (`nl-NL`). - **English:** British (`en-GB`) and American (`en-US`). - **Finnish:** Finland (`fi-FI`). - **French** (`fr-FR`). - **German** (`de-DE`). - **Italian** (`it-IT`). - **Japanese** (`ja-JP`). - **Korean:** South Korea (`ko-KR`). - **Polish** (`pl-PL`). - **Portuguese:** Brazilian (`pt-BR`) and European (`pt-PT`). - **Romanian:** Romania (`ro-RO`). - **Russian** (`ru-RU`). - **Spanish:** Spain (`es-ES`). - **Swedish:** Sweden (`sv-SE`). Choose your first language during onboarding, then add more from **Settings → My Languages**. Your plans, progress and flashcards stay separate for each language, including regional variants. On self-hosted installations, `AVAILABLE_TARGET_LANGUAGES` controls which options are available. Your native language is a separate choice made during registration. It is used for translations, explanations and tutor feedback to support you while you learn. The interface language is another independent choice in **Settings**. It controls menus and interface text without changing your native language or the languages you study. Maintainer implementation guides: [adding a study language](specs/add-target-language.instructions.md) and [adding an interface or native language](specs/add-ui-native-language.instructions.md). ## Linux host: Redis memory overcommit Redis requires `vm.overcommit_memory=1` on the host for reliable background saves (RDB snapshots). Without it, a `fork()` under low memory can fail and unsaved data may be lost on restart. Run once on the server: ```bash sudo sysctl vm.overcommit_memory=1 echo "vm.overcommit_memory = 1" | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf ``` The first command applies the setting immediately; the second persists it across reboots. This is a host-level setting and cannot be applied from within the container without elevated privileges. ## Reverse proxy requirement (real-time conversation) > [!IMPORTANT] > Production voice conversation needs **HTTPS** for microphone access and **WebSocket routing** to > the backend. Next.js HTTP rewrites do not forward WebSocket upgrades. Route `/ws/*` to the backend listener configured in Compose, including `/ws/conversation`. The production frontend derives its WebSocket URL from `window.location`. Browser microphone access requires a [secure context](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Secure_Contexts) such as HTTPS or localhost; ordinary HTTP access through a server IP does not provide it. ## Configuring TTS & STT TTS and STT are required services, selected independently via `.env`. - `TTS_PROVIDER=local` uses Kokoro-FastAPI; `openai` uses OpenAI TTS; `gemini` uses Gemini TTS. - `STT_PROVIDER=local` uses faster-whisper; `STT_PROVIDER=openai` uses OpenAI Whisper. - `OPENAI_API_KEY` is required when either service uses OpenAI. - `GEMINI_API_KEY` is required only when `TTS_PROVIDER=gemini`. ### Local speech The default local services in `docker-compose.yml` are configured for NVIDIA GPUs: ```env TTS_PROVIDER=local STT_PROVIDER=local ``` `TTS_VOICE` selects the Kokoro voice. FreeLingo does not automatically select a Kokoro voice from the study language. OpenAI TTS supports the language-aware pronunciation guidance described in the [speech specification](specs/speech-services.instructions.md). For CPU-only local deployment, select CPU images, remove GPU reservations, and use a smaller Whisper model as documented in [the Docker specification](specs/docker.instructions.md). ### Cloud speech OpenAI providers require no local GPU or speech containers: ```env TTS_PROVIDER=openai STT_PROVIDER=openai OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... ``` `OPENAI_TTS_MODEL` selects the OpenAI TTS model. Settings offers female/male choices for both cloud TTS providers, with independent preferences. Operators configure the OpenAI mappings through `OPENAI_TTS_FEMALE_VOICE` and `OPENAI_TTS_MALE_VOICE`. `OPENAI_TTS_VOICE` selects the default logical choice. Existing provider-name preferences are ignored until a new choice is saved. Legacy `tts-1`/`tts-1-hd` models require compatible voice mappings; see the [speech specification](specs/speech-services.instructions.md). Remove the corresponding `kokoro` and/or `whisper` service blocks from your deployment Compose file when using cloud providers for those services; changing the provider variables alone does not remove their GPU reservations. For Gemini TTS, select `TTS_PROVIDER=gemini` and set `GEMINI_API_KEY` on the backend. `GEMINI_TTS_MODEL` selects the model; configurable female/male voices produce native WAV audio. STT remains an independent local or OpenAI choice. Settings stores the Gemini voice preference separately from OpenAI. OpenAI speech services reuse `OPENAI_API_KEY` when OpenAI is also the LLM provider. See [.env.example](.env.example) for available settings and [the speech-services specification](specs/speech-services.instructions.md) for provider contracts. ## Development See [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md) for the repository-local toolchain and validation workflow on macOS and glibc-based Linux. It covers setup, focused tests, static checks, and environment recreation. ## Contributing Bug reports, feature suggestions, documentation improvements, and code contributions are welcome. - [Contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) — read before opening an issue or pull request. - [Code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) — community expectations. By opening a pull request you accept the [Contributor License Agreement](CONTRIBUTOR_LICENSE_AGREEMENT.md). ## License Distributed under the [GNU Affero General Public License v3](LICENSE). Organisations that need to deploy FreeLingo without the AGPL's copyleft obligations can obtain a **commercial licence**. See [COMMERCIAL_LICENSE.md](COMMERCIAL_LICENSE.md) or [get in touch](https://freelingo.app) via the contact form. ## Author **Arturo Carretero Calvo** — [@artcc](https://github.com/artcc)
